factors.name: Forecast Channel Margin Rotation
factors.description: Computes a sector-neutral cross-sectional wedge between 21-bar EPS-estimate revisions and revenue-estimate revisions, each scaled by its own trailing forecast level. The wedge is weighted by cross-sectional income quality so that margin-implied revisions are strongest when reported earnings are more cash-backed.
factors.trading_idea: Analysts revise revenue and EPS forecasts through distinct channels: an EPS revision that is strong relative to the contemporaneous revenue revision signals a reassessment of margins, mix, or operating leverage rather than merely a sales-volume change. Investors often anchor on the more salient revenue narrative and discount margin revisions as temporary, particularly when the issuer has weak cash conversion evidence; the factor therefore emphasizes the EPS-versus-revenue revision wedge when income quality is high. This is falsifiable: high-quality firms with positive relative EPS revisions should outperform firms with negative wedges over the next six trading days, while the relationship should weaken or disappear among low-income-quality firms. The edge can persist because forecast-model changes are sparse, heterogeneous across analysts, and difficult to arbitrage immediately without distinguishing durable unit-economics revisions from transitory accounting effects.

factors.name: Fresh Revision Reaction Inertia
factors.description: Cross-sectionally scores newly available EPS-consensus revisions and scales them by the gap between the revision direction and the stock's volatility-normalized same-day price response. A large positive score is an upgrade that the market has not yet fully incorporated, while a large negative score is an underreacted downgrade.
factors.trading_idea: Fresh analyst EPS revisions contain information, but the same-day price response is often incomplete when investors must distinguish a durable earnings reset from routine estimate maintenance. The signal buys upgrades and shorts downgrades only when the contemporaneous move is muted relative to the stock's own recent volatility, targeting delayed information assimilation rather than generic momentum. The edge can persist because discretionary investors and benchmarked institutions process revisions and rebalance with delay; it is falsified if muted-response revisions have no stronger 6-bar continuation than revisions whose price response was immediately complete.

factors.name: Operational Coherence Muted-Response Drift
factors.description: Ranks firms on reporting dates by the joint direction of gross-margin and cash-conversion-cycle changes, then emphasizes updates whose trailing sector-relative price reaction has not already moved in the same direction. Higher values represent positive operational coherence that remains under-assimilated.
factors.trading_idea: A simultaneous improvement in gross margin and cash-conversion efficiency is a costly-to-fake operational-state transition: it indicates that a firm is both producing more profitable revenue and converting it into cash more efficiently. Investors often process headline earnings and revenue before integrating profitability with working-capital information, so firms whose coherent operational update receives little same-direction idiosyncratic price response should continue to reprice over the following week. This is falsified if joint margin/working-capital improvements with muted initial reactions do not outperform equally strong updates that were immediately priced; the edge can persist because it requires point-in-time accounting-state changes, a cross-field coherence test, and conditioning on the market's initial response rather than merely screening for quality.

factors.name: Silent Confirmation Valuation Drift
factors.description: Ranks a decayed signed estimate-revision signal after a long update silence, requiring alignment with a preceding sector-relative price move. The signed confirmation is amplified when sector-relative log PE is directionally consistent with the revision.
factors.trading_idea: The parents' negative realized signs suggest that silent, price-leading estimate revisions are not generally exhaustion events: they can certify an already emerging fundamental narrative to investors who act only after consensus catches up. This child therefore trades in the direction of a long-silent revision that confirms a substantial sector-relative price move, but conditions its strength on valuation being coherent with the revision: expensive names receiving upgrades and cheap names receiving downgrades are treated as persistent repricing regimes rather than generic reversals. Price leadership alone cannot distinguish durable narrative validation from noise, while valuation alone has no near-term catalyst; their interaction identifies consensus confirmation that broadens participation in an already valuation-consistent regime.

factors.name: Standardized EPS Revision Impulse (jitter)
factors.description: Computes the five-day cumulative EPS-estimate revision and scales it by the issuer's trailing 126-day RMS daily revision size. It ranks fresh, statistically unusual upgrades above unusual downgrades while assigning neutral scores to stale consensus levels.
factors.trading_idea: The parent likely overfit by combining infrequently updated accounting translation measures with estimate changes, creating a stale and noisy interaction. This child isolates the more universal mechanism: a newly large EPS-consensus revision relative to that issuer's own revision noise is a high-information forecast innovation that institutional investors assimilate gradually as analysts, mandates, and portfolio rebalancing propagate the update. The edge persists because consensus changes arrive asynchronously and are costly to continuously arbitrate across a broad equity universe; it is falsified if unusually large positive and negative standardized EPS-revision impulses do not predict correspondingly signed returns over the next six trading days.

factors.name: Industry Revision Adoption Gap
factors.description: Computes a leave-one-out industry consensus-revision state with a smooth exponential memory, then favors names whose own estimates have remained inactive and whose industry-adjusted price has not yet moved materially. The final signal is sector-demeaned to reduce broad sector-news exposure.
factors.trading_idea: Analyst revisions often propagate through economically linked firms because analysts update the directly affected company first and subsequently revise adjacent industry models after checking read-through, competitive effects, and management commentary. The signal identifies firms with a fresh, persistent industry-peer revision state, little recent revision activity in their own consensus, and muted idiosyncratic price adjustment; these are likely slow adopters rather than exhausted revision recipients. The edge should persist because updating firm-specific earnings models is costly and asynchronous across sell-side coverage, while a falsification would be that peer revision pressure has no incremental ability to predict six-day returns after conditioning on the firm's own revisions and industry-adjusted price move.

factors.name: Industry-Residual Estimate Persistence
factors.description: Computes robustly scaled EPS and revenue estimate-update impulses, retains only coherent same-direction updates through a causal exponential decay, and industry-neutralizes the resulting consensus signal. Long names have the strongest positive firm-specific estimate persistence relative to their industry peers.
factors.trading_idea: Industry-wide estimate changes largely reflect already-observed macro, commodity, or sector news, whereas the component of a coherent EPS-and-revenue revision that is unusual versus direct industry peers is more likely firm-specific information that investors must verify and gradually incorporate. The factor retains recent estimate innovations through a short decay kernel, then removes the contemporaneous industry consensus component rather than using price trend as a phase classifier. The edge should persist because validating issuer-specific operational information is costly and because analyst updates arrive asynchronously, while broad industry news is easier for arbitrageurs to recognize and trade immediately.

factors.name: Quadrature Participation Diffusion
factors.description: Computes a causal trailing Fourier component of returns and log-volume innovations at an eight-bar cycle, then ranks directional return components only when volume has coherent positive phase lag. High scores represent positive price components leading delayed participation; low scores represent negative components leading delayed participation.
factors.trading_idea: A directional price cycle whose associated volume cycle lags in phase indicates that price discovery has begun before broad trading participation has caught up. Unlike ordinary momentum, the signal only takes exposure when trailing return-volume cross-spectral coherence is high and the phase relationship implies delayed participation, so it targets gradual attention and execution diffusion over the fixed six-bar horizon. The edge should persist because portfolio managers, passive reallocators, and dispersed discretionary investors respond to observed price moves with delay rather than instantaneously coordinating volume; it is falsified if price-leading-volume episodes do not outperform same-sign price components over the next six bars.

factors.name: Covariance-Budget Rebalance Overhang
factors.description: Construct an equal-weight market return, estimate each stock's short-window and long-window covariance with that market, and normalize the covariance contribution by its market-cap share. The factor is the negative cross-sectional rank of the short-versus-long covariance-budget innovation, with extreme observations damped by rolling volatility normalization.
factors.trading_idea: Risk-managed portfolios react not only to a stock's standalone volatility but also to an increase in its covariance contribution to the broad market portfolio. A rapid rise in market covariance relative to market-cap weight creates a predictable sell-pressure overhang from volatility-targeting, risk-parity, and constrained mean-variance allocators whose estimates and execution are staggered; high positive covariance-budget innovations are short candidates and negative innovations are long candidates. The mechanism is falsified if covariance-contribution innovations do not forecast relative returns after conditioning on realized volatility, beta, and recent market return; the natural counterparties are slower-moving fundamental investors willing to absorb these non-informational reallocations.

factors.name: Common-Shock Covariance Capacity Overhang
factors.description: The signal shorts stocks with a positive short-versus-long market-covariance-budget innovation, conditional on a statistically large market down move and weighted by low trailing turnover capacity. It is inactive outside common downside-shock states.
factors.trading_idea: A negative broad-market shock activates volatility-targeting and risk-budget deleveraging, but the resulting sale program is concentrated in names whose market-covariance contribution has risen most sharply. Price pressure should be strongest where normal turnover capacity is low relative to market capitalization, because dealers and discretionary investors cannot immediately absorb the reallocation. The edge persists because the risk-manager demand is mechanical and execution is staggered; it is falsified if covariance-budget increases during downside market shocks do not underperform specifically among low-turnover-capacity names over the next six bars.

factors.name: Delivery-Vetoed Terminal Schedule Fade
factors.description: Computes a signed terminal-flow score from schedule regularity, absorption, path pinning, and close-location agreement, then attenuates it when fresh coherent estimate revisions, delivery, and a value-quality anchor corroborate the direction of the price pressure.
factors.trading_idea: Persistent, low-entropy price-volume pressure with muted marginal impact and repeated same-side closes identifies a mature mechanical execution schedule whose terminal inventory transfer is prone to reverse over the next week. The child fades that pressure only when fresh coherent estimate revisions and realized earnings/cash-flow delivery fail to validate its direction; credible delivery vetoes the fade because the same apparent terminal pressure can instead be informed repricing. Neither parent alone separates mechanical schedule completion from economically justified price discovery at the moment when the two observationally look most similar.

factors.name: Revision-Anchored Schedule Terminal Reversal
factors.description: Ranks the signed estimate-revision direction only when a prior regular, revision-aligned participation kernel is present and the current opening gap against the revision is reclaimed on elevated volume. Higher values identify likely terminal buy-program completion and are expected to precede lower six-day returns.
factors.trading_idea: The parents' negative realized signs suggest that a revision-aligned reclaim during regular abnormal participation is often not the start of information diffusion, but the terminal bar of a scheduled transfer: the opening dislocation draws in liquidity, and the regular-session reclaim completes the remaining parent order. The child therefore requires pre-existing, directionally revision-aligned kernel pressure and regular participation before an auction-opposed reclaim occurs. This interaction isolates execution completion after a temporary auction displacement, a state neither a generic metaorder signal nor a generic revision reclaim can identify alone, and predicts a six-day reversal as dealer inventory and temporary impact unwind.

factors.name: Impact-Impedance Pressure Release
factors.description: Measures signed close-location pressure during abnormal volume and reverses it only when recent return-per-participation is compressed relative to its own trailing baseline, a proxy for directional flow being absorbed with low impact.
factors.trading_idea: Abnormal directional participation that produces unusually little price displacement indicates that liquidity providers or latent counterparties are absorbing a mechanical execution program rather than repricing on information. When this low-impact pressure persists for several bars, the temporary inventory imbalance is likely to release over the next week: absorbed selling predicts a rebound and absorbed buying predicts a pullback. This is falsifiable if the conditional return spread disappears after controlling for contemporaneous return, realized range, abnormal volume, and market beta; it can persist because hidden liquidity, dealer inventory management, and scheduled institutional execution are not directly observable from daily bars and cannot be frictionlessly arbitraged during the program.

factors.name: Weekly Execution Echo Coherence
factors.description: Measures excess weekly-lag return coherence relative to one-day autocorrelation, then applies it only to current return impulses confirmed by unusually high volume. The signal is sector-neutralized and cross-sectionally ranked, favoring positive high-volume impulses in names with recurring five-day execution echoes.
factors.trading_idea: Some institutional execution schedules recur on a weekly trading-day cadence because portfolio rebalances, cash-flow deployment, and broker algorithms are organized around recurring operational calendars. A current high-participation return should therefore predict a same-direction echo roughly one week later only when the stock has previously exhibited materially stronger five-day return autocorrelation than ordinary one-day persistence; this is falsifiable by testing whether the conditional effect vanishes after controlling for current return, volume surprise, and conventional momentum. The edge can persist because the relevant schedules are fragmented across investors and costly to front-run: traders must wait for repeated, stock-specific phase coherence rather than trading a visible calendar effect unconditionally.

factors.name: Clustered Participation Inventory Release (jitter)
factors.description: Constructs a signed participation event from abnormal log volume multiplied by close location within the daily range, then fades fresh events only when a trailing exponentially decayed intensity shows prior same-signed participation clustering. The result is sector-neutralized and cross-sectionally ranked.
factors.trading_idea: Repeated high-participation closes near the same end of the daily range proxy a self-exciting execution episode: informed or liquidity-driven parent orders attract continuation trading, but also accumulate dealer and liquidity-provider inventory. Once a fresh event arrives after several same-signed events, the marginal price impact is increasingly temporary and inventory rebalancing should reverse the move over the next week. The edge should persist because daily bars do not reveal the execution schedule, the inventory transferred across intermediaries, or whether a volume burst is isolated versus part of a clustered episode; it is falsified if same-signed prior participation does not strengthen subsequent reversal after conditioning on the current event.

factors.name: Marked Excitation Cooling Reversal
factors.description: Constructs fast and slow exponentially decayed Hawkes-style intensities of positive and negative volume-marked return shocks. It fades elevated upside excitation only after its fast intensity falls below its slow intensity, while buying the analogous completed downside-excitation state, sector-neutralized cross-sectionally.
factors.trading_idea: The parent likely entered explosive price-volume episodes while excitation was still accelerating; its negative IC emerging after several days is consistent with reversal occurring only after the burst begins to cool. This child models a completed self-exciting episode: a large slow-moving signed, volume-marked return intensity combined with a lower fast intensity indicates that endogenous participation is decaying while the price remains displaced. The hypothesis is falsifiable: conditional on comparable recent signed returns and volume, names with positive cooling residuals should underperform and negative cooling residuals should outperform over six days; the effect should disappear if cooling merely reflects ordinary information diffusion. Arbitrage is limited because distinguishing a completed reflexive burst from a continuing news-driven trend requires waiting for participation decay, and shorting the residual upside tail remains risky.

factors.name: Marked Close-Location Program Coherence
factors.description: Computes volume-surprise-weighted close-location marks and scales their recent signed average by directional coherence, the ratio of net marked flow to total marked-flow magnitude. High positive values identify sustained high-participation closing demand, while negative values identify sustained supply.
factors.trading_idea: A sequence of unusually high-volume bars that repeatedly closes near the same end of its intrabar range is treated as a coherent marked order-flow process, rather than as a collection of unrelated price moves. Persistent directional coherence indicates an unfinished institutional demand or supply program whose inventory transfer continues over the next week; alternating close-location marks instead indicate two-sided liquidity provision and receive little weight. The edge should persist because daily-bar observers cannot distinguish the ultimate informed or liquidity-driven source of the program in real time, while execution constraints spread the transfer across multiple sessions; it is falsified if the signal has no six-day predictive power after controlling for trailing return and relative volume.

factors.name: Sector-Residual Flow Branching Drift
factors.description: Computes fast-versus-slow Hawkes-style excitation in abnormal signed volume, then sector-neutralizes the directional branching innovation. High values identify stocks with idiosyncratic buy-flow escalation beyond the contemporaneous sector flow state.
factors.trading_idea: The parent’s absorption-reversal signal appears partly redundant with existing flow and impact factors. This child instead treats rapid, same-direction marked-volume excitation that is unusually strong relative to the stock’s simultaneous sector excitation as evidence of an idiosyncratic informed order-splitting process, which should continue rather than reverse over the next week. The hypothesis is falsifiable: sector-residual buy-side branching innovations should precede positive six-day returns and corresponding sell-side innovations negative returns; broad sector-wide bursts should have materially weaker predictive power. The edge can persist because daily-bar investors cannot directly observe the hidden parent order, while market makers rationally update adverse-selection beliefs only gradually as the sequence of abnormal prints arrives.

factors.name: Concordant Peer Disclosure Burst Gap
factors.description: Computes leave-one-out industry peer EPS-and-revenue surprise marks, exponentially accumulates their signed and event-count intensities, and rewards coherent bursts whose implication is not reflected in the receiver's recent industry-relative return. Event detection is explicitly based on point-in-time changes, preventing quarterly fields carried forward between releases from being repeatedly counted as new events.
factors.trading_idea: A cluster of same-industry earnings and revenue surprises with concordant signs is a stronger signal of a shared demand, cost, or competitive shock than an isolated peer release. The child treats such clusters as a marked self-exciting disclosure burst and buys receivers whose industry-relative prices have not yet absorbed the coherent peer information, while shorting the opposite case. This is falsified if concordant multi-peer disclosure bursts do not predict receiver-relative returns after controlling for the receiver's immediate relative response; the edge can persist because investors initially trade the reporting firms, while mapping a burst's common implication onto non-reporting peers requires costly exposure analysis.

factors.name: Inventory-Vetoed Excitation Reversal
factors.description: Computes signed cooling completion from fast versus slow volume-marked return intensities, then scales its reversal signal by a sigmoid gate that is large only when accumulated flow-impact residual is opposite to the completed burst direction. The output is cross-sectionally ranked each day.
factors.trading_idea: A cooling marked price-volume burst is normally a reversal candidate because self-exciting participation has stopped replenishing while the price remains displaced. However, the reversal should be weaker when dealer inventory still contains untransmitted flow in the same direction: positive residual buy pressure can force subsequent dealer hedging upward, while negative residual sell pressure can extend a decline. The child therefore trades completed excitation only when the inventory-capacitance state vetoes continuation, separating exhausted reflexive bursts from bursts backed by latent execution demand.

factors.name: Industry Earnings Cross-Excitation Underreaction
factors.description: Builds a signed, exponentially decayed leave-one-out industry intensity of fresh EPS-surprise events, then weights it by the receiver's muted contemporaneous return response. High values identify quiet stocks exposed to positive peer earnings-news cascades; low values identify quiet stocks exposed to negative cascades.
factors.trading_idea: Earnings surprises are clustered within industries because suppliers, competitors, and customers reveal correlated demand and margin information at different reporting dates. A fresh surprise from several industry peers raises the conditional probability that an initially quiet firm's fundamentals will be reassessed over the following week; the signal only trades names whose price has not already moved materially, separating information diffusion from already-assimilated common news. The edge can persist because heterogeneous earnings calendars, analyst coverage constraints, and costly fundamental attribution delay the mapping of peer disclosures into each receiver's valuation.

factors.name: Signed Flow Intensity Imbalance
factors.description: Computes positive and negative marked return-volume events from standardized daily returns and abnormal log volume, then forms an exponentially decayed Hawkes-style intensity imbalance. Cross-sectional rank favors names experiencing clustered, price-confirmed buy-flow over clustered sell-flow.
factors.trading_idea: Clusters of unusually high-volume, same-direction daily price moves are a daily-bar proxy for self-exciting institutional order flow: one informed or mechanically scheduled trade raises the probability of further same-side trading. The child goes long names with greater exponentially decayed positive marked-flow intensity than negative intensity, rather than attempting to infer issuer motives from sparse quarterly accounting branches. The edge should persist for several days because large orders are fragmented and information is incorporated gradually; it is falsified if intensity imbalance has no positive monotonic relation with six-bar residual returns after controlling for contemporaneous volatility and volume.

factors.name: Private Placement Capacity Diffusion
factors.description: Ranks fresh positive equity-issuance disclosures that coincide with a positive disclosed cash change and high ROIC, then favors events where price holds near the daily high despite below-normal public volume. A short causal decay keeps the signal focused on the first week of institutional-placement information diffusion.
factors.trading_idea: The parent’s realized sign suggests that low secondary-market participation after a fresh issuance is not necessarily failed demand: when issuance is accompanied by a disclosed cash increase, it can indicate a privately absorbed placement whose institutional validation has not yet diffused into public trading. High-ROIC issuers can deploy this new capital productively, so a near-high close with muted public volume is evidence that the placement avoided a public distribution overhang rather than evidence of weak absorption. The prediction is falsifiable: positive six-day returns should be concentrated in fresh positive issuance events with contemporaneous cash proceeds and high ROIC, while issuance without cash proceeds or with poor operating returns should not exhibit the effect. The edge can persist because filing-level financing details and the distinction between private absorption and public selling pressure are processed more slowly than the initial daily bar response.

factors.name: Sell-Arrival Impact Compression Repair
factors.description: Ranks stocks by the interaction of recent downside-volume arrival intensity and the inverse of their realized downside price impact per arrival. High scores identify active selling that is being absorbed with comparatively little price damage.
factors.trading_idea: Large downside-associated trading arrivals normally require a substantial price concession to clear. When elevated sell-arrival intensity produces unusually little downside impact per unit of relative volume, latent demand is absorbing supply and the remaining seller inventory is likely depleted, creating a six-bar repair. This is falsifiable: positive forward returns should concentrate in names with both high recent sell-arrival intensity and low realized impact per arrival, while high-impact selling episodes should not repair; the edge persists because absorption and inventory transfer are not directly observable from daily bars and liquidity providers require time to recycle acquired inventory.

factors.name: Distributed Sector Inventory Relaxation
factors.description: Computes a five-day sector-relative return overhang accumulated only during synchronized, directionally incoherent sector range-and-volume shocks. It fades that overhang when the affected name shows persistent above-normal participation and non-endpoint closes, indicating distributed execution rather than a thin-side directional vacuum.
factors.trading_idea: Sector-wide simultaneous range and turnover shocks with mixed constituent signs are consistent with basket-level inventory transfer rather than uniform information revelation. The parent’s strongest effect at three bars suggests that its one-day displacement signal was realized too quickly; this child instead accumulates only the residual displacement created by several days of elevated participation, which should leave a slower inventory overhang that repairs over the fixed six-day horizon. The hypothesis is falsifiable: positive accumulated sector-relative overhangs should have negative six-day residual returns, especially when closes remain away from range endpoints; the effect should be weak for isolated one-day shocks or endpoint-confirmed directional moves. The edge can persist because execution schedules, dealer inventory constraints, and uncertainty about whether a sector shock is informational prevent arbitrageurs from immediately separating temporary basket pressure from genuine repricing.

factors.name: Idiosyncratic Attention Burst Reversal
factors.description: Ranks the reversal of close-location direction when an individual name has an abnormal volume burst and unusually concentrated recent volume, downweighting dates when many names simultaneously experience volume bursts. High scores correspond to isolated sell-pressure episodes expected to rebound; low scores correspond to isolated buy-pressure episodes expected to fade.
factors.trading_idea: The parent’s negative realized IC implies that an edge-close during temporally concentrated volume is more often terminal execution pressure than underreacted information: a buy or sell program can push the close to a bar boundary while dealers temporarily warehouse inventory. This child isolates episodes that are idiosyncratic rather than market-wide, because broad synchronized volume shocks are more likely to contain common information whereas isolated bursts are more plausibly institutional rebalancing, forced flow, or liquidity-demand shocks. The edge should persist because the resulting inventory transfer and temporary price impact unwind gradually over several sessions as liquidity providers recycle risk; it is falsified if boundary-close reversals are not stronger for low-breadth, abnormal-volume entropy collapses than for broad participation shocks.

factors.name: Fundamental-Anchor Extrapolation Penalty
factors.description: Ranks a composite of earnings yield, free-cash-flow yield, ROIC, and low asset growth, then subtracts an industry-relative 15-bar price-run-up penalty that is largest for weak-fundamental names. Positive relative moves are volatility-standardized and only affect the score when they represent potential extrapolative overvaluation.
factors.trading_idea: Investors extrapolate a stock's industry-relative price run-up most aggressively when that run-up is unsupported by a slow-moving fundamental anchor of value, profitability, and conservative investment. The child retains the parent’s economically interpretable exposures but replaces its unstable fitted premium posterior with a direct asymmetric conditioning rule: only positive relative-price moves in fundamentally weak names are penalized. The edge should persist because benchmarked investors and attention-driven traders can chase salient relative winners before quarterly fundamentals are fully reweighted; it is falsified if the conditional penalty does not improve the six-bar return spread versus the unconditioned fundamental anchor, especially in the weak-anchor/high-run-up short leg.

factors.name: Salient Accrual Growth Extrapolation
factors.description: Industry-neutral short signal for fresh, high-attention growth narratives whose revenue growth is not supported by operating cash flow, receivables, or cash-conversion-cycle changes. It is strongest among expensive names using price-to-sales and free-cash-flow-yield valuation conditioning.
factors.trading_idea: Investors tend to extrapolate salient revenue-growth headlines, especially when unusually high turnover makes the narrative broadly visible, while giving less weight to contemporaneous deterioration in operating-cash-flow growth, receivables growth, or cash-conversion-cycle efficiency. The child shorts expensive names with this revenue-to-cash-conversion divergence shortly after a quarterly update, because subsequent scrutiny of working-capital funding needs should correct the overly optimistic growth interpretation over the next six days. The edge can persist because interpreting accrual and working-capital disclosures is costly and heterogeneous, while shorting glamour names is riskier than mechanically trading the headline. Falsifiably, the negative forward return spread should be concentrated in fresh, high-turnover updates with high sales multiples and should disappear when cash-flow growth and working-capital metrics confirm revenue growth.

factors.name: Headline-Margin Conflict Repricing
factors.description: Ranks fresh reporting events by the disagreement between revenue surprise and EPS surprise, industry-neutralises the disagreement, and activates it only for above-median price-to-sales names. High values identify expensive firms with positive headline revenue delivery but comparatively weak earnings delivery.
factors.trading_idea: A fresh revenue beat paired with an EPS miss creates a salient headline-growth narrative while revealing that incremental sales are not translating into profitability. Investors and news-driven flows initially overweight the revenue headline, especially for high price-to-sales firms where growth extrapolation is central to valuation, and the profitability shortfall is incorporated over the following week. The edge persists because interpreting the revenue-versus-earnings conflict requires accounting for cost structure and valuation context rather than reacting mechanically to the headline; it is falsified if high-sales-multiple firms with fresh revenue-beat/EPS-miss conflicts outperform rather than underperform over the next six bars.

factors.name: Unconfirmed Growth Extrapolation Premium
factors.description: Ranks stocks by a sector-relative valuation-weighted gap between a standardized 10-day price run-up and contemporaneous EPS/revenue estimate revisions, with greater weight for weak income quality. High values indicate expensive, low-quality price extrapolation not supported by analyst fundamentals.
factors.trading_idea: Investors can extrapolate a recent price run-up in expensive growth firms even when both EPS and revenue consensus have not corroborated the move. The child shorts this joint price-versus-estimate mismatch most strongly where profitability quality is weak, because low-quality earnings make optimistic narratives especially fragile. The edge should persist over six days because growth uncertainty, benchmark-driven ownership, and short-sale frictions delay correction; it is falsified if high-mismatch names do not underperform, or if their returns are equally poor when analyst revisions jointly confirm the price move.

factors.name: Peer Downgrade Resilience Fade
factors.description: Ranks expensive stocks with strong short-run returns relative to sector peers when those peers have recently suffered EPS-estimate reductions and the stock has no offsetting own upgrade. The score is active only during fresh sector-peer downgrade episodes.
factors.trading_idea: A stock that temporarily outperforms its sector while peers receive fresh EPS-consensus downgrades can be a delayed receiver of sector-level information rather than a genuinely differentiated winner. The effect should be strongest for expensive names without a confirming own estimate increase: investors extrapolate the relative-price resilience before revising the stock's exposure to the same industry demand or margin shock. The edge persists because analyst revisions arrive discretely across covered firms and investors process peer read-throughs gradually; it is falsified if resilient, expensive, non-upgraded names do not underperform following fresh peer downgrade clusters.

factors.name: Absorbed Downside Variance Innovation
factors.description: Estimate a causal EWMA baseline for downside semivariance from daily close-to-close returns and measure the current negative-return variance innovation relative to that baseline. Multiply the negative innovation by the normalized close location within the daily high-low range, favoring stocks with an extreme volatility shock but a close near the bar high.
factors.trading_idea: Negative return shocks create disproportionately large volatility innovations because risk-targeting, margin, and VaR-constrained investors mechanically reduce exposure after losses. A large downside semivariance surprise that is followed by a strong close-location recovery indicates that forced selling was absorbed rather than supported by continued information-driven selling, creating a short-horizon rebound opportunity. The mechanism is falsified if high downside variance innovations with end-of-day recovery continue to underperform rather than mean-revert over the next six sessions.

factors.name: Industry-Residual Downside Cluster Extinction
factors.description: Computes industry-demeaned daily returns, measures a recent burst in idiosyncratic downside semivariance relative to its trailing baseline, and rewards bursts whose current downside energy is rapidly decaying. It intentionally replaces same-day wick/volume confirmation with a multi-day residual-volatility extinction state.
factors.trading_idea: A burst of downside variance that is idiosyncratic to a stock rather than shared by its industry is more likely to reflect forced liquidation, dealer-inventory stress, or a temporary local liquidity vacuum than a sector-wide information shock. The child goes long only after that downside-energy burst demonstrably cools, treating declining excitation as evidence that the selling cluster has become subcritical and that the remaining inventory overhang should unwind over the next week. The edge can persist because liquidity providers and constrained sellers adjust inventory gradually, while arbitrageurs cannot immediately distinguish an extinguishing forced-flow episode from genuinely adverse private information. This is falsifiable: high-scoring names should outperform over six bars, whereas names whose residual downside energy remains elevated should not.

factors.name: Fundamental-Vetoed Idiosyncratic Extinction Repair
factors.description: Computes exponentially decayed intensity of negative industry-residual returns, scores unusually elevated prior intensity that is now decaying, and suppresses the signal after a newly disclosed negative EPS surprise. High values identify likely transient forced-flow repairs rather than post-earnings information incorporation.
factors.trading_idea: The parent mechanism identifies a stock-specific downside-excitation cluster that is fading, but fading volatility alone cannot distinguish exhausted forced selling from a rational repricing after bad earnings news. This child retains the industry-residual, self-exciting sell-pressure extinction signal while vetoing it when a fresh negative EPS-surprise release has occurred during the repair window. The interaction has edge because inventory-driven liquidation should rebound as the Hawkes-like sell intensity decays, whereas fundamentally informed selling should continue to drift even when immediate volatility temporarily cools.

factors.name: Asymmetric Semivariance Pressure Acceleration
factors.description: Computes market-relative negative-return semivariance normalized by trailing volatility, then measures whether its short-horizon exponentially weighted intensity exceeds its slower intensity. High values identify accelerating idiosyncratic downside-pressure regimes and are expected to precede lower returns.
factors.trading_idea: The parent’s failed reversal interpretation suggests that a high close after a downside shock is often not genuine absorption: during a cluster of idiosyncratic negative shocks, it can instead be a temporary rebound while constrained sellers continue to delever. This child measures acceleration in downside semivariance relative to a slower baseline, a daily-bar proxy for asymmetric self-exciting sell pressure rather than a single-bar endpoint pattern. The edge should persist because margin, volatility-targeting, and inventory-risk constraints force gradual execution and make arbitrageurs reluctant to immediately warehouse names with rising downside jump intensity; it is falsified if sector-neutral names with the strongest downside-pressure acceleration do not underperform over the next six bars.

factors.name: Asymmetric Downside Excitation Intensity
factors.description: Computes a causal, exponentially decayed intensity of unusually large downside-return events, where each event is normalized by trailing downside volatility. High values identify names in an active asymmetric downside-excitation regime and are expected to precede lower six-bar returns.
factors.trading_idea: The parent’s negative realized sign suggests that apparent sell-program cooling is often not supply completion but a late-stage observation of self-exciting downside trading. Large negative returns increase the near-term intensity of further negative-return arrivals through margin constraints, volatility targeting, stop-loss execution, and impaired liquidity provision; this excitation decays gradually rather than reversing immediately. The edge should persist because these mechanical feedback loops are distributed across heterogeneous investors and cannot be instantaneously arbitraged away when short-side capacity and inventory are constrained.

factors.name: Covariance-Relieved Downside Exhaustion
factors.description: Computes a signed downside-excitation curvature score and conditions it on a causal, volatility-normalized innovation in covariance contribution per unit market-cap weight. It rewards downside-burst deceleration when covariance-budget pressure is easing and penalizes accelerating downside excitation when that pressure is still rising.
factors.trading_idea: A decelerating downside-volatility burst is only a reliable six-bar rebound signal when the stock's market-covariance budget is no longer rising: risk-managed portfolios have largely completed the correlated deleveraging that originally amplified the selloff. If covariance-budget pressure remains elevated or is still increasing, the same apparent local exhaustion can be temporary because staggered volatility-targeting and risk-parity selling continues. The interaction therefore distinguishes genuine forced-sale completion from a transient pause inside a broader common-shock liquidation regime, which neither standalone signal can identify.

factors.name: Balance-Sheet Buffered Stress Rebound
factors.description: Ranks financially resilient names experiencing an elevated, self-exciting idiosyncratic downside cluster while broad downside semivariance is unusually high. Solvency is measured cross-sectionally from cash coverage and debt-to-assets, with sector demeaning to reduce persistent industry composition effects.
factors.trading_idea: Market-wide downside-volatility bursts trigger mechanically correlated deleveraging, but an unusually large idiosyncratic sell shock in a financially resilient firm is more likely to be temporary inventory liquidation than a durable deterioration in solvency. The child therefore identifies clustered relative downside pressure during systemic stress and scales it by cash/liquidity strength and low leverage, rather than relying on an intraday closing-location reversal. The edge should persist for roughly six sessions because risk-budget reductions and dealer inventory transfer unwind gradually, while arbitrage is limited during stress by funding constraints and the difficulty of distinguishing forced sales from adverse information in real time. It is falsified if resilient firms with clustered idiosyncratic sell pressure during market-stress episodes do not outperform weaker-balance-sheet firms facing comparable pressure.

factors.name: Fragile Tail Backlog Completion Reversal
factors.description: Ranks recovered, abnormal-volume downside excursions after conditioning them on financial fragility, excess sector downside-tail beta, current sector stress, and a recently elevated but decelerating delayed-volume backlog. High values identify likely terminal forced-sale absorption and predict positive six-bar returns.
factors.trading_idea: A recovered intraday downside probe is most informative when it occurs in a financially fragile name with elevated sector-downside exposure, because those names are more likely to have faced genuine forced selling rather than random intraday noise. The child requires evidence that the prior delayed-volume liquidation backlog is now cooling, turning Parent B's continuation state into an execution-completion clock and Parent A's wick into direct evidence that residual supply has been absorbed. Parent A alone cannot distinguish a terminal absorption from a still-active sell program, while Parent B alone is directionally bearish during an unresolved backlog and misses the reversal created when that backlog decays into a high-participation recovery.

factors.name: Dual Disclosure Attention Gap Drift
factors.description: Detects fresh quarterly reports whose EPS and revenue surprises have concordant cross-sectional directions. It favors positive disclosures with weak immediate price and volume response, and assigns negative scores to similarly underreacted negative disclosures.
factors.trading_idea: A quarterly disclosure is more credible when earnings and revenue surprises point in the same direction, because the two independently observed channels reduce the probability that the result is accounting noise or a one-off classification effect. When such concordant news receives little abnormal trading attention and only a muted same-day price response, dispersed investors have not yet fully processed the higher-quality information, producing six-bar drift in the disclosure direction. This is falsifiable: conditional on dual-sign agreement, future returns should increase monotonically with the fundamental-price reaction gap and decrease with abnormal turnover; the edge persists because processing multi-line disclosures is costly and institutional attention is capacity constrained around clustered reporting dates.

factors.name: Opening Gap Refill Elasticity
factors.description: Compute the signed overnight gap, its intraday refill fraction from open to close, and abnormal volume relative to recent volume. Rank stocks by a signed failed-auction score that is high for heavily traded upward gaps that refill downward and low for heavily traded downward gaps that refill upward.
factors.trading_idea: A large opening gap is more informative when the subsequent daily auction fails to sustain it despite substantial trading activity. A positive gap that closes near or below the prior close after elevated volume indicates that opening liquidity was temporarily depleted and passive liquidity later absorbed the buy imbalance; the symmetric case applies to negative gaps. The edge should disappear if gap-fade episodes do not exhibit materially greater subsequent mean reversion than equally sized gaps with persistent closing pressure.

factors.name: Cash-Validated Auction Continuation
factors.description: Computes the gap-direction continuation signal implied by an abnormal opening gap that closes against its direction, then weights it by fresh estimate-revision magnitude and directional agreement between the revision and cash-flow validation. High scores identify credible fundamental-information states whose opening-auction rejection is interpreted as absorbed execution pressure rather than reversal.
factors.trading_idea: An opening gap that is rejected intraday is not necessarily a failed price discovery event: when a fresh analyst revision is corroborated by cash-flow quality, the rejection can instead reflect informed institutions absorbing temporary auction liquidity and completing execution during the continuous session. The revision-and-cash state separates fundamental demand from purely mechanical opening dislocations, while the auction pattern identifies the names where that demand is temporarily obscured by execution pressure. Neither parent has this edge alone: the auction pattern is ambiguous without a credibility state, and a credible revision does not identify when transient opening liquidity offers a delayed continuation entry.

factors.name: Revision Release Completion Hazard
factors.description: Ranks a decayed, issuer-standardized EPS-revision impulse only when prior endpoint pressure was opposite to the revision and its abnormal-volume intensity is now declining. The completion gate targets the slower post-schedule release phase rather than contemporaneous flow opposition.
factors.trading_idea: A consensus revision should have its clearest six-day effect after an opposed high-participation execution episode has begun to decay, rather than while that pressure remains active. The decaying pressure is a daily-bar proxy for a metaorder approaching completion: liquidity-demand price displacement fades, allowing the public revision to be incorporated in its fundamental direction. This is falsifiable by testing whether revision-direction returns are materially stronger after opposed endpoint-pressure decay than after equally large revisions with persistent or accelerating pressure; the edge can persist because execution completion is uncertain and costly to arbitrage from coarse daily volume and OHLC information.

factors.name: Cadenced Endpoint Idiosyncratic Absorption Reversal
factors.description: Ranks the expected reversal of persistent signed scheduled pressure when endpoint placement agrees with the pressure direction, both intrabar and close-to-close impact efficiency have weakened, and the day's range shock is not market-wide. The factor is long absorbed sell programs and short absorbed buy programs.
factors.trading_idea: Scheduled abnormal participation with fading intrabar impact identifies a program increasingly absorbed by replenishing liquidity, as in Parent A. Parent B's endpoint state is used as a confirmation variable rather than a standalone reversal signal: absorption is most credible when the persistent displacement is repeatedly expressed at the close endpoint but close-to-close impact per unit participation is weak. The signal suppresses episodes in which range shocks are synchronized across the market, because broad liquidity evaporation or common information shocks are more likely to continue than an idiosyncratic dealer-inventory unwind.

factors.name: Revision Participation Inelasticity Drift
factors.description: Ranks persistent standardized EPS-estimate revisions, weighted by abnormal volume and downweighted when the contemporaneous two-day price response is already large relative to trailing volatility. The signal is high for upward revisions, and low for downward revisions, whose information appears absorbed rather than immediately repriced.
factors.trading_idea: Consensus revisions should continue to drift when they arrive during unusually high trading participation but produce little immediate price displacement. This combination indicates that liquidity-demanding execution and offsetting limit-order supply are absorbing the information, so the estimate change has not yet been fully incorporated into the price. The prediction is falsifiable: revision-direction returns over the next six days should be strongest in the high-participation, low-impact subset and weak or absent after equally sized revisions that immediately move price. The edge can persist because daily OHLCV cannot identify the side, identity, or remaining duration of the institutional execution schedule that creates the temporary absorption.

factors.name: Regular Schedule Absorption Continuation
factors.description: The signal estimates signed close-location-weighted relative volume, subtracts its contemporaneous normalized price transmission, and retains it most strongly when relative volume has been elevated but regular across recent days. It ranks positive absorbed buy schedules above negative absorbed sell schedules.
factors.trading_idea: Persistent institutional execution is more likely to continue over the next week when participation is both elevated and temporally regular, rather than being a one-day information or liquidity shock. If this regular signed participation has moved the close only modestly relative to the stock's normal daily range, liquidity providers have absorbed the flow and the remaining execution schedule should create short-horizon directional drift. This is falsified if regular, elevated, low-impact signed participation has no positive six-day return conditional on its sign; the edge can persist because the latent parent order and dealer inventory are not directly observable in daily bars, while trading against an unfinished schedule entails adverse-selection and execution-risk costs.

factors.name: Flow Extinction Inventory Reversal
factors.description: Ranks names with decaying previously elevated signed close-location/relative-volume flow and unusually compressed current ranges. The score buys after extinguishing sell programs and sells after extinguishing buy programs.
factors.trading_idea: The parent’s negative realized IC suggests that muted-impact directional flow is more often the terminal phase of an execution program than evidence of a still-active informed schedule. This child identifies a previously elevated, regular signed-flow state that is now decaying while the daily range remains compressed: passive liquidity has absorbed the program, and dealer inventory/risk transfer subsequently produces a reversal opposite to the prior flow direction over the fixed six-bar horizon. The edge should persist because daily bars reveal the completed-flow footprint only imperfectly, while inventory redistribution and the removal of one-sided execution demand occur over several sessions; falsifiably, the reversal should disappear when either prior flow elevation, subsequent flow extinction, or range pinning is removed.

factors.name: Compressed-Depth Acceptance Drift
factors.description: Ranks signed close-location pressure on unusually high volume, gated by prior relative-range compression. Positive values identify upward acceptance through depleted offer-side depth; negative values identify downward acceptance through depleted bid-side depth.
factors.trading_idea: Displayed and latent liquidity is most vulnerable after several unusually narrow ranges, when repeated small trades can consume resting depth without moving price materially. A subsequent high-participation bar that closes near one extreme is treated as acceptance through the depleted side of the book rather than a rejected probe, so the remaining scheduled flow should continue to move price over the next six sessions. The hypothesis is falsified if high-volume directional closes following compression revert as often as analogous bars without prior compression; the edge can persist because daily-bar participants cannot directly observe the latent depth already consumed by fragmented execution.

factors.name: Issuance Cadence Unpaid Pressure
factors.description: Ranks names with recent positive net-stock-issuance innovations whose normalized sell pressure is persistent and regular, while price declines have not fully reflected that pressure. High values represent likely continuing issuer-distribution pressure and are expected to precede lower six-bar returns.
factors.trading_idea: Fresh disclosed net issuance identifies an issuer-related supply overhang, but the six-bar effect should be strongest specifically when daily sell participation has become regular rather than merely large. Regular, low-dispersion sell pressure with weak contemporaneous price transmission is consistent with a scheduled execution program repeatedly replenishing supply into available liquidity; the untransmitted component should be marked down as the program continues. This remains difficult to arbitrage because the true issuer/executor schedule and remaining inventory are latent, while daily-bar participants observe only noisy realized volume and price response; falsifiably, the downside should disappear when sell-cadence coherence breaks or when the issuance event becomes stale.

factors.name: Participation Phase-Lock Drift
factors.description: Computes the normalized eight-bar directional displacement and weights it by positive rolling cosine coherence between returns and unexpected log-volume. Long signals identify upward displacement repeatedly accompanied by above-normal participation; short signals identify the symmetric selling pattern.
factors.trading_idea: A persistent institutional execution program produces an unusual phase-lock between daily return direction and participation shocks: returns occur in the same direction on days when volume is unexpectedly high relative to the stock's own recent trading clock. This differs from plain momentum because directional displacement is traded only when it is corroborated by abnormal participation, a proxy for unresolved informed or inventory-motivated demand rather than a low-liquidity price fluctuation. The hypothesis is falsified if stocks with positive (negative) return-volume phase-lock over the prior eight bars do not earn positive (negative) six-bar residual returns after cross-sectional ranking. The edge can persist because identifying a genuine execution schedule requires conditioning jointly on a stock-specific volume baseline and multi-day price-volume coherence, while arbitrageurs face uncertain metaorder duration and finite capacity in the names receiving the demand.

factors.name: Idiosyncratic Impact-Cluster Cooling Clock
factors.description: Builds a residualized downside-impact event process from negative returns, liquidity-cost surprises, and volume surprises. It ranks names with a large recent idiosyncratic event cluster whose fast exponential intensity has fallen below its slower intensity, indicating execution completion rather than continuing distress.
factors.trading_idea: Constrained liquidation creates a clustered sequence of idiosyncratic downside bars with unusually high range-per-dollar-volume, whereas fundamental repricing should not systematically stop once the local order-flow burst cools. The child measures an exponentially decayed downside-impact intensity and goes long only after a previously elevated idiosyncratic cluster is demonstrably cooling, when dealers can replenish inventory and the temporary impact debt is repaid over the fixed six-bar horizon. The edge persists because the completion of a large seller's execution schedule and liquidity-provider inventory rebalancing are not instantaneously observable from daily bars; it is falsified if high scores do not exhibit both declining subsequent impact intensity and positive six-bar sector-relative returns.

factors.name: Sector Commonality Inventory Debt Release
factors.description: Measures exponentially accumulated signed abnormal participation, then longs previously sold names and shorts previously bought names when participation and intrabar impact are both cooling during a common sector liquidity-cost shock. The sector condition replaces the parent's unstable idiosyncratic residual gate with a smoother common-inventory state.
factors.trading_idea: A persistent signed, abnormal-participation imbalance builds dealer inventory debt when its price impact is absorbed rather than permanently transmitted. The child conditions that completion signal on a sector-wide liquidity-cost shock, because correlated liquidity withdrawal makes dealers more likely to warehouse and subsequently unwind inventory across related names. The edge should persist because the inventory transfer and its gradual relaxation are not directly observable from daily bars and cannot be instantaneously arbitraged without bearing liquidity risk; falsifiably, high-score names should show declining participation and normalising sector liquidity cost before their positive six-day markout.

factors.name: Fast Liquidity Replenishment Completion
factors.description: Fades sector-relative three-day price displacements when two-sided cancelling bar pressure coincides with a recent impact shock that has decayed rapidly back toward its normal level. The completion gate is designed to select short-lived inventory shocks rather than persistent adverse-selection episodes.
factors.trading_idea: A price displacement accompanied by alternating, cancelling pressure is more likely to be a dealer-inventory transfer than informed directional trading. The child trades only when an elevated range-per-volume impact shock has substantially normalized within three bars, identifying a completed rather than merely beginning liquidity-replenishment episode; this timing should concentrate the rebound into the configured six-bar horizon instead of retaining the parent's slower 24-bar tail. The edge persists because liquidity providers and execution algorithms manage inventory gradually after a transient shock, while daily-bar participants cannot directly observe the latent replenishment state. This is falsifiable: conditional six-bar reversal should be materially stronger after fast, near-complete impact normalization than after equally large price moves with persistent or only partially relaxed impact.

factors.name: Latent Liquidity Absorption Underreaction
factors.description: Ranks a three-bar average of signed close-to-open range displacement, weighted by a trailing liquidity-absorption score: log-volume surprise minus log-range surprise. High values identify upward directional bars whose participation is unusually large for their realized range; low values identify the analogous downward state.
factors.trading_idea: A large directional close-to-open displacement occurring on unusually high participation but an unusually compressed intrabar range indicates that latent liquidity absorbed substantial one-sided flow without fully repricing the asset. This differs from plain momentum: the signal is active only when volume is high relative to realized range, a daily-bar proxy for hidden depth and informed execution rather than a mechanically large return. The residual underreaction should continue over the next six sessions as the remaining metaorder is executed or liquidity providers update adverse-selection estimates; the edge persists because arbitrageurs must absorb inventory and adverse-selection risk before that repricing completes. The hypothesis is falsified if high-volume, low-range directional bars do not have more same-direction six-bar returns than otherwise similar directional bars with normal volume-to-range elasticity.

factors.name: Overnight-Intraday Disagreement Repair (jitter)
factors.description: Ranks stocks by the direction of their idiosyncratic overnight gap when that gap is opposed intraday, scaled by the smaller of the two moves and activated only when intraday volume is below its trailing norm. High scores indicate positive overnight gaps rejected on weak volume; low scores indicate negative gaps rejected on weak volume.
factors.trading_idea: Overnight gaps and intraday returns are generated by partially segmented trader populations: overnight repricing reflects dispersed information and inventory transfer, while the daytime move can reflect liquidity-demanding institutional execution. When a large idiosyncratic overnight move is substantially opposed during a low-confirmation-volume session, the daytime rejection is less likely to represent broad information aggregation and the subsequent return should repair toward the overnight direction. This is falsified if, conditional on opposite-signed overnight and intraday moves, low-volume disagreement does not predict six-bar returns in the direction of the overnight gap. The effect can persist because it requires separating two trading sessions and conditioning the disagreement on name-specific volume confirmation, which is not captured by simple daily reversal signals.

factors.name: Relaxing Idiosyncratic Impact Markout
factors.description: Ranks names by the opposite of their recent directional return only when a recent sector-relative liquidity-impact shock has peaked and is now decaying. It is sector-neutralized cross-sectionally so that it targets idiosyncratic inventory release rather than broad sector repricing.
factors.trading_idea: A large stock-specific range-per-dollar-volume shock accompanied by a directional markout can reflect an inventory-motivated execution program rather than information, but the parent acted while that program was still active. This child waits for a measurable decline in the idiosyncratic impact shock after a recent peak, treating that deceleration as evidence that constrained selling or buying capacity has begun to clear while the price remains displaced. The expected six-bar return is a repair of the residual markout; the edge can persist because inventory completion is not directly observable from daily bars and arbitrageurs must bear adverse-selection risk before the liquidity state is confirmed.

factors.name: Fresh Earnings Response Residual
factors.description: On fresh EPS-report dates, computes the cross-sectional gap between standardized EPS surprise rank and same-day volatility-normalized return rank. High values are favorable surprises that received too little immediate price recognition; low values are unfavorable surprises with too little immediate discounting.
factors.trading_idea: A newly reported earnings surprise contains public information, but the same-day price response is often incomplete because investors face attention, interpretation, and portfolio-rebalancing frictions. The factor buys positive surprises whose volatility-normalized initial reaction is weak relative to the cross-section, and shorts negative surprises that are insufficiently discounted. The edge should persist for several days because daily-bar investors cannot immediately distinguish temporary liquidity-driven price moves from the economically relevant portion of a new earnings disclosure; it is falsified if the surprise-minus-response residual has no positive six-day cross-sectional IC after conditioning on fresh report dates.
